analysis.title: Diversify beyond the AI rally (UBS House View - Daily Asia)
key_insights: US equities extended gains on Tuesday 10/27 as tech rallied: the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index rose 3.6% and the Nasdaq rose 1.2%.

Tech fundraising was the main focus on Wall Street. Broadcom arranged a USD 63bn deal to finance chip purchases, SpaceX signed a roughly USD 40bn equipment-finance lease, and Meta raised its equity fundraising to USD 97.5bn.

UBS stays constructive on AI demand as a key growth engine and expects hyperscaler September-quarter results in the coming days to give more evidence on the sustainability and monetization of that demand.

High expectations and wide differences in company outcomes raise single-stock concentration risk. UBS recommends broadly diversified equity portfolios and says long-term growth investors should also consider Power and resources and Longevity.

Power and resources: investment in AI and electrification raises the need for data centers, power generation, grids and related infrastructure. UBS favors a selective approach, preferring businesses with visible multi-year demand, credible capacity expansion, disciplined balance sheets and the ability to protect margins amid elevated input costs and interest rates.

Longevity: aging populations and clinical innovation support demand. Recent earnings point to moderating medical procedure demand, but low penetration and this year's valuation reset support the longer-term case. UBS is also positive on obesity treatments as greater supply and lower pricing broaden patient access.

UBS is positive on Eurozone equities (manufacturing recovery, structural investment, improving operating leverage). It says Asian valuations are at multi-decade lows with AI investment and a cyclical recovery supporting earnings, and expects Japanese equities to benefit from AI capex, cyclical improvement and corporate reform.

EURUSD fell for a fourth straight session to about 1.11 as the DXY rose to 102. UBS reads this as a US dollar rebound rather than Europe-specific stress, even though French bond yields stabilized after Moody's did not downgrade France.
UBS expects EURUSD to recover toward 1.16 by year-end and likes selling the downside in EURUSD for yield pickup. It does not expect a broader European debt crisis.

sector_views.rationale: AI and electrification investment drive demand for data centers, power generation and grids, with an improving automation cycle and stronger metals prices as additional support. UBS favors a selective approach.
Demographics, clinical innovation and inelastic demand support the theme despite moderating medical procedure demand. The sector had a significant valuation reset this year.
UBS is constructive on structural AI growth but warns of high expectations, wide dispersion in company outcomes and single-stock concentration risk.

earnings_insights: Hyperscalers report September-quarter results in the coming days. UBS expects them to show evidence on the sustainability and monetization of AI demand.
Earnings due 10/28: Microsoft, Alphabet, Ford and GE Vernova.
Recent health care earnings point to moderating medical procedure demand.

macro_indicators.interpretation: The dollar index has gained against six key US trading partners' currencies amid renewed confidence in US tech stocks.
Fourth consecutive daily decline, attributed by UBS to US dollar strength rather than Europe-specific stress.
UBS expects a recovery in EURUSD by year-end.
